jobs.title: Support Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Launching a mobile service requires stitching together carriers, regulations, payments, and support across markets. We’ve built the platform. The next challenge is scaling operations so customers go live smoothly, stay healthy, and their learnings feed back into the product.

You will own the end-to-end support experience across the customer lifecycle, from launch readiness and implementation through post-launch optimization. You will partner closely with customers to design and run their support motion, identify the moments that drive contacts and dissatisfaction, and turn those insights into playbooks and improvements that make every new launch smoother and every user experience better. You will operate with high autonomy and report to the Head of Support.

This role is for someone who thrives in complexity, communicates confidently with senior customer stakeholders, and uses AI as default leverage to move faster and build better.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Be the face of Gigs with customers. Serve as the primary point of contact across pre-sales, implementation, and post-launch. Build the kind of relationships where customers call you first when something goes wrong—because they trust you to fix it.

 - Dig into the data. Track activation funnels, identify drop-off and degradation patterns, run root cause analyses on performance issues. Turn what you find into clear, actionable recommendations—not dashboards that collect dust.

 - Take field insights back to the product. You'll see where the platform breaks in practice before anyone else does. Structure that knowledge and bring it to Product and Engineering in a way they can act on. You're the closest thing to a field reporter we have.

 - Build AI into how you work. Use AI tools to automate recurring tasks, accelerate analysis, prototype lightweight internal tooling, and generally move faster than headcount would otherwise allow. This is a working expectation, not a perk.

 - Know the platform end to end. Get deep into how Gigs works—provisioning, billing, support tooling, connectivity infrastructure. You should be able to explain any part of the system to a customer and diagnose any part of it when it fails.

 - Build what scales. Write the runbooks, design the workflows, and document what you learn so that the next deployment goes faster than the last. What you build should outlast your direct involvement.

 - Keep things moving. Help cross-functional teams stay coordinated and accountable. Unblock what needs unblocking. Reduce friction without creating bureaucracy.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in a demanding operational environment—strategy & operations, bizops, management consulting, technical account management, or somewhere else where you had to figure out how to get hard things done with imperfect information. You've operated under pressure. You know what it feels like to own something that matters.

 - You are self-driven and relentlessly proactive. You don't need someone to hand you a problem definition. You find the problem, form a view on how to solve it, and start moving. We'd rather tell you to slow down than push you to speed up.

 - AI is part of your working stack. You use AI tools daily—for analysis, automation, building internal tooling, accelerating research. You can point to specific things you've built or automated that didn't exist before you made them. This is a working expectation, not a cultural point.

 - You can read the room and the data. Comfortable running SQL, building in spreadsheets, working across BI tools. You can translate a data finding into a business decision and communicate it clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.

 - Technically curious. You don't need to be an engineer. But you need to be the kind of person who reads API documentation for fun, asks sharp questions in engineering conversations, and understands enough about how systems work to be dangerous in a good way.

 - Credible with customers. You can run an external meeting with a customer's executive team, manage post-launch relationships with follow-through and care, and represent Gigs in a way that builds trust rather than dependency.

 - High ownership, low ego. You juggle context across multiple workstreams without dropping threads. You take pride in making complex things work reliably, not in getting credit for it. When something is yours, it gets done.

Bonus points if

 - You have experience in telecoms, fintech, or B2B SaaS—especially anything touching connectivity, payments, or platform operations.

 - You've worked in a customer-facing implementation or technical account management role and know what good looks like.

 - You've built or improved internal tooling, reporting infrastructure, or automated workflows using AI or no-code tools.

 

Salary Range: $140,000 - $190,000

jobs.title: Head of Operations
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

As Head of Operations you will own 3 areas:

First, the path from signed contract to live revenue. When a partner signs for one of our product lines (Gigs for Work, Connect, API), marketing, implementation, product, partner management, and go-to-market each own a piece of what happens next, and nobody owns the whole thing. Launches take longer than they should. You will own that path end to end and turn it into a process we can repeat.

Second, the company's operating cadence. Gigs is approaching 200 people, and the planning cycles, business reviews, and decision forums need a full-time owner. The founders do this work today, which pulls them away from strategy. You will take it over, and make sure the goals leadership sets reach every team that has to deliver them.

Lastly, you will also run Business Operations, and set the operational standards that our functional ops teams work to. This role sets the pace and the bar for how Gigs operates. You will build what does not exist yet, not maintain what already does.

Compensation: $300K+ and a significant equity package. 


WHAT YOU WILL OWN

1. Customer and partner lifecycle, from signed deal to live revenue

 - Own the process that takes a partner from signed contract to live, revenue-generating product.

 - Build one repeatable launch process with clear stages, named owners, timelines, and go-live readiness criteria, so no launch gets reinvented.

 - Stitch together the handoffs between go-to-market, partner management, implementation, product, and support, and close the gaps where work currently stalls.

 - Shorten time to launch as the playbook matures, and make that number visible to the company.

 - Build the feedback loops, internal and external, that show where launches get stuck.

2. Company operating cadence and business reporting

 - Design and run the rituals that keep Gigs coordinated: annual planning, quarterly goal cycles, leadership syncs, and business reviews.

 - Run a goal-setting framework teams use and trust, and make sure goals travel all the way down, so an engineering manager's team knows what it is building and how it ladders up.

 - Build a single source of truth for company-level KPIs, with a monthly and quarterly business review process that has a consistent format and clear ownership.

 - Run clear decision forums so issues surface early and do not stall.

 - Build the operational layer that catches and routes day-to-day escalations, so founders stop being the default path.

3. Operational standards across functions

 - Operations capability at Gigs sits inside functions: support ops, growth ops, people ops, connectivity ops, and later product, legal, and talent ops. That is healthy. Without a layer above it, each function optimises locally, tooling fragments, and cross-functional dependencies get dropped.

 - Set the shared operating principles, tooling conventions, and process standards that functional ops teams apply in their own domains.
   
   - Keep reporting consistent and non-duplicative across those teams.
   
   - Work with connectivity ops on reliability: clear SLAs, escalation paths, and quality monitoring for provisioning and activation.

 - Over time there is a path for functional ops leads to report into this role, consolidating operational leadership under one owner.

4. Business Operations

 - Own the BizOps team, which covers the work that does not fit inside one function.

 - Expansion operations: the operational backbone for launching new markets and products, working with go-to-market, product, and partnerships so new bets land well.

 - AI operations: Gigs' internal leverage from AI. Find where AI compresses work, pilot the tooling, embed the workflows, and prove the efficiency.

 - Special projects: the high-priority cross-functional projects that sit above any single team, where speed and a dedicated owner matter more than org lines.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You have built operational infrastructure at a high-growth startup or scaleup, ideally through a 250+ person scaling phase. You built it, you did not inherit it.

 - You straddle two layers that rarely sit in one person. You can run real operations (playbooks, process design, launches, ops teams) and you can think strategically about where the business should go. Strong on one and thin on the other will not work here.

 - You have owned a process that crosses many functions and made it hold, including the handoffs, the owners, and the follow-through.

 - Strong planning and process instincts. You can design a planning cycle, run a business review, and build accountability systems without over-engineering them.

 - Analytically sharp. You define the metrics, work with the data, and build the reporting yourself rather than queueing a data team.

 - You set pace. You are direct, you close loops, and you raise the bar for how the people around you work. This is a culture-setting hire.

 - A track record of using AI as a real operational lever, with efficiency you can point to rather than tools you can list.

 - Helpful: exposure to international expansion, market launches, multi-jurisdiction operations, telecom, payments, or API-first infrastructure.

 - Based in or moving to New York or San Francisco.

jobs.title: Business Operations
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

As a Business Operations (BizOps) hire, you’ll play a critical role in solving high-impact strategic and operational challenges across the company. You’ll work directly with the founder’s office and leadership team to turn vision into execution, bringing data-driven insights and operational rigor to our most pressing priorities.

This is a unique opportunity to help shape the trajectory of a fast-growing startup by building the BizOps function from the ground up. You’ll operate at the intersection of strategy, operations, finance, and product — a trusted problem-solver and thought partner to teams across the business.

What you will do

 - Partner with the executive team to identify and drive forward high-leverage strategic initiatives across departments (e.g. go-to-market, pricing, international expansion, planning).

 - Build scalable business processes to support rapid growth — from first principles through implementation.

 - Define key metrics, build dashboards, and deliver insights that drive better decisions across the company.

 - Structure and solve ambiguous business problems, distilling complex data into actionable recommendations.

 - Lead cross-functional initiatives and ensure clear communication and accountability across stakeholders.

 - Own strategic planning cadences, including annual planning, quarterly reviews, and operating rhythms.

 - Serve as a force multiplier for the leadership team, helping translate vision into scalable execution.

 - Run toward whatever is most pressing. Jump on the urgent, ambiguous, or unowned problems and drive them to resolution, whatever the function.

 - Use AI to work faster and go deeper: automate analysis, accelerate research, prototype workflows, and build leverage the rest of the team can reuse.

What we are looking for

 - 3-5+ years of experience in a high-performance environment such as management consulting, investment banking, private equity, or in a BizOps / Strategy & Operations / roles at a fast-scaling tech company.

 - Proven track record of tackling unstructured problems and driving initiatives from 0 to 1.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; you’re comfortable modeling in Excel and wrangling data in tools like Looker or SQL.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills — you can drive alignment and clarity across senior stakeholders.

 - Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

 - A collaborative, low-ego mindset and the ability to influence without authority.

 - A genuine curiosity for how things work and a deep desire to make them better.

 - AI fluency. You already use AI tools in your daily work and have sharp instincts for where they add leverage: speeding up analysis, research, drafting, and building repeatable workflows.

 - A bias to run toward problems. You gravitate to the hardest thing in the room and are happy to work on anything that moves the business, regardless of scope or title.

Salary range: $130,000 - $160,000 annually + equity

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)

jobs.title: Growth Strategy and Ops
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Gigs has built a multi-market, multi-product embedded connectivity business, and we're looking for someone to own the operating system the Growth team runs on. This is a high-leverage, cross-functional role sitting at the intersection of strategy, data, and execution, responsible for making the Growth org faster, smarter, and more cohesive.

You will operate with high autonomy and report to the VP of Growth, while working closely with Finance, Legal, and functional leads across GTM, Customer Success, Implementation, and Marketing.

This role is for someone who thrives in complexity, communicates confidently with senior stakeholders, and uses AI as default leverage to move faster and build better.

 

What you will do

 - Own the operating cadence of Growth. Run planning cycles, reporting rhythms, and cross-functional coordination across GTM, Customer Success, Implementation, and Marketing, so Growth runs as one function.

 - Build what lets knowledge travel. Write the playbooks, runbooks, and documentation that take what works in one region and make it work everywhere else. What you build should outlast your direct involvement.

 - Own the data and reporting infrastructure. Build the systems that tell the Growth team what's working and where to focus next.

 - Lead the AI and tooling stack. Make sure the team is actually using AI to multiply output.

 - Drive strategic projects end-to-end. Market expansion, segmentation, GTM playbooks, from framing the problem to shipping the output.

 - Keep the function moving. Unblock what needs unblocking across a multi-market, multi-product Growth team that's operating faster than its infrastructure can handle.

 

What we are looking for

 - 4+ years in a demanding operational environment — biz ops, strategy & ops, management consulting, or growth ops at a fast-scaling company. You've operated under pressure and know what it feels like to own something that matters

 - You are self-driven and relentlessly proactive. You don't need someone to hand you a problem definition. You find the problem, form a view, and start moving. We'd rather tell you to slow down than push you to speed up

 - AI is part of your working stack. You use AI tools daily—for analysis, automation, building internal tooling, accelerating research. You can point to specific things you've built or automated that didn't exist before you made them.

 - You can read the room and the data. You can translate a data finding into a business decision and communicate it clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.

 - You're a generalist who goes deep. Comfortable moving between a data problem, a process problem, and a strategic framing problem in the same week.

 - High ownership, low ego. You juggle context across multiple workstreams without dropping threads. You take pride in making complex things work reliably, not in getting credit for it. When something is yours, it gets done.

Bonus points if

 -   You have experience in telecoms, fintech, or B2B SaaS - especially anything touching connectivity or payments. 

 -   You've built or improved internal tooling or automated workflows using AI or no-code tools.

 -   You've operated across multiple markets or regions and know what it takes to make something work globally, not just in one office.

Salary Range: £85,000 - £110,000
(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

As Chief of Staff to the CEO, you are our CEO's force multiplier. You make the CEO and the company move faster and decide better.

You work at the center of Gigs: strategy, the leadership team's operating cadence, board and investor work, and the highest-priority projects in the company. You take first cuts on ambiguous problems, turn rough direction into sharp narratives, and build the mechanisms that keep a fast-scaling company aligned as it grows. When something matters and has no owner, you own it.

This is a senior role. You will sit in rooms with the leadership team, the board, and investors, and you will be trusted to act on the CEO's behalf. It is also a role of high leverage and low ego: your job is to make other people's output better, often without your name on it.

Salary range: $270K - $300K


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Be the CEO's thought partner. Take structured first cuts on the hardest questions. Synthesize context, run the analysis, frame the options and trade-offs, and recommend a path. Give our CEO a sharper starting point than a blank page.

 - Build and run the founders' transmission layer. Turn the founders' priorities into execution across the company. Capture decisions, drive follow-ups, close loops, and make sure nothing important waits on them. This is the operational spine of the founders' office, and you own it.

 - Own board and investor work. Build board decks and investor materials that tell a clear, honest story. Shape the fundraising narrative and the numbers behind it. Prepare the founders for every board meeting and investor conversation so they walk in ready.

 - Write in the founders' voice. Turn rough storylines into polished decks and memos for all-hands, builder meetings, leadership reviews, and external moments.

 - Lead special projects end to end. Take on the urgent, cross-functional, often confidential work: fundraising, org design, new market entry, key hires, the occasional fire. Drive them to done.

 - Act as proxy. Represent the founders in meetings when they can't be there. Carry decisions, unblock teams, and be a reliable channel between the founders and the company.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Senior generalist track record. 8+ years across strategy consulting, banking, VC, or senior strategy/ops roles in high-growth tech. You have run workstreams, teams, or functions, and people trust your judgment.

 - Executive-grade communication. Writing and slides that tell a clear story and drive a decision. You can brief a board and rally a room of builders with the same material.

 - Sound judgment under ambiguity. You make progress with imperfect information and competing priorities. You make the call and own it.

 - Business and financial fluency. You are comfortable with a model, a cap table, a board narrative, and the metrics that run the business. You can hold your own with Finance and investors.

 - High ownership and discretion. Deadline-driven, detail-obsessed, able to run many workstreams without dropping balls. Trusted with the company's most sensitive information.

jobs.title: Strategic Partner Manager, EU
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Gigs is the operating system for mobile services - a platform that powers the next generation of connectivity products. Our partners are not customers. They are fintechs, retailers, and B2B SaaS companies who embed our platform into their own products and ship it to millions of end users. As a Strategic Partner Manager, you'll own and grow our most important European relationships.

This isn't a standard account management role. It's part commercial growth, part customer success, part business strategy. You'll act as a trusted advisor to executives at fast-scaling fintechs, while ensuring Gigs becomes a critical growth lever for their business. Your mission: drive revenue, retention, and long-term partnership value.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own commercial and operational performance across a portfolio of European partners — NRR and compounding ARR are your headline numbers

 - Build the financial model for each partner: pricing, unit economics, growth scenarios. Carry it into rooms with partner CxOs and senior leadership

 - Work shoulder to shoulder with your partner’s Product team on funnels, app placement, and product surfaces inside the partner's stack - improving the product will be a critical lever of growth

 - Successfully sell and run multiple launches per partner each year: new geographies, new product lines, promotions. Coordinate Implementation, Partner Marketing, Legal, Support and Connectivity to ship them

 - Develop a deep understanding of each partner's business, use cases, and KPIs. Anticipate needs, surface risks, and guide them as they scale into new markets and geographies

 - Be the internal advocate for what partners need next, and the external advocate for what Gigs is building

 - Build trust deep inside partner organisations: with PMs, ops leads, CxOs, and founders

 - Balance commercial ownership with genuine customer success — adoption, value delivery, and retention matter as much as the renewal


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Must-have

 - Commercial ownership. You've carried revenue targets, negotiated contracts, and tracked metrics like NRR, GRR, and ARR. You can build a financial model from scratch and defend it in a room with a CFO.

 - B2B2C experience. You've owned relationships with large, complex customers who serve millions of end users — and understand the dual focus on the business customer and their consumers.

 - Product depth as a growth driver. You understand how product decisions drive growth — funnels, app placement, and how a PM is targeted for consumer conversion. You can hold your own in a product conversation, and you've influenced a partner's product direction in service of growth outcomes. Not implementation depth — but genuine product fluency.

 - Multi-stakeholder complexity. You have a track record of managing partner or customer relationships that span PMs, ops leads, CFOs, and founders simultaneously. Not transactional account management.

 - Fintech experience. You've partnered with fintech or financial services companies and can navigate regulatory complexity, integration depth, and the pace of innovation in this industry.

 - Emotional intelligence and influence. You can build trust with C-level stakeholders, navigate tough conversations with empathy, and drive alignment across complex organisations.

 - Builder mentality. You know what it takes to thrive in a fast-scaling company where playbooks are still being written. You bring agility, creativity, and genuine comfort with ambiguity.

Nice-to-have

 - Early consulting background followed by a move into partnerships or commercial — a strong positive signal and a near-guarantee of commercial rigour (reference profiles within the Partner Success team)

 - Experience in telco, connectivity, or embedded finance

 - AI-native working style: you use the best tools available to multiply your output and quality

 

Salary Range:

Netherlands: €115,000 - €130,000 basic - UK: £100,000 - £115,000 basic

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)

jobs.title: Strategic Partner Manager, US
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Regulatory & Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Gigs is growing fast across markets, and we need someone to build and operationalize regulatory and compliance systems to make that growth possible. This isn't just a compliance role; it's also a builder's role. You'll build workflows, design processes, ship tooling, and work across Business Development, Legal, Product, and Engineering. You'll enable how we launch new markets and how we stay compliant across the current footprint.

This is our first hire in this area. You'll shape the function from scratch.

Salary range:

 - UK: £90,000 - 140,000

 - US: $180,000 - 220,000

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Build our operational infrastructure for market expansion. Own the end-to-end process for launching in new markets: regulatory readiness, product compliance checks, internal workflows, and cross-functional coordination.

 - Turn regulatory requirements into systems. Work with Legal to understand what's required, then build clear, repeatable processes that the team can follow without bottlenecks. Don't just document rules -- make them run.

 - Automate before it breaks. Partner with Engineering and Product to embed controls into our systems early. Reduce manual work. Build things that scale before they need to.

 - Own filings, registrations, and reporting. Manage our ongoing regulatory obligations across jurisdictions. Track deadlines. Make sure nothing slips.

 - Track compliance health. Define metrics, build dashboards, flag problems early, fix them fast.

 - Keep documentation sharp. Maintain policies, procedures, and process docs that are clear, findable, and up to date.

 - Stay ahead of regulatory changes. Monitor new requirements across target markets and subject matters. Build implementation plans before deadlines arrive.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of regulatory and compliance experience, ideally at a telecom company or other regulated tech business (fintech, payments).

 - You've built or scaled compliance systems in a fast-moving environment. You know how to take a messy process, structure it, and make it run.

 - Ability to research and interpret legal and regulatory requirements.  Experience and familiarity with common compliance areas, including consumer protection, privacy (e.g., GDPR, CPRA, LGPD), and infosec.

 - Real experience with compliance or regulatory work -- as someone who's turned regulatory requirements into working processes across areas like product compliance, vendor risk, or cross-border operations.

 - Comfortable with tooling: GRC systems, databases, workflow automation. You don't need to be an engineer, but you can build things using AI.

 - Strong communicator. You can explain a regulatory filing to an engineer and a process gap to a lawyer.

Bonus if you have experience in fintech, B2B SaaS, data privacy, or hold a law degree.

jobs.title: Gigs for Work Partner Manager
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Gigs for Work is Gigs' enterprise offering - we help businesses give their employees access to world-class connectivity. We're looking for a Partner Manager to own the commercial success of our GfW enterprise accounts: ensuring partners launch well, grow fast, and stay.

This is a high-ownership, relationship-heavy role sitting at the intersection of commercial, product and operations. You'll be the primary relationship owner for a portfolio of enterprise GfW accounts, taking accounts from launch through to expansion, renewal and strategic planning. You're stepping into a nascent existing book of business, with a chance to play a fundemental role at the beginning of the development of this critical vertical.

The GfW motion is distinct from Gigs' core partner model. Your counterparts aren't product teams embedding connectivity into consumer apps, they're HR leads, IT directors, procurement teams and C-suite at enterprises deploying connectivity across their workforce. You need to speak their language, understand how they measure success, and make Gigs a strategic vendor in every account.

 


WHAT YOU WILL DO

Commercial ownership

You hold the number. NRR and ARR across your GfW account portfolio are yours to grow. That means proactively identifying expansion opportunities (new employee cohorts, new geographies, new use cases), running renewal conversations with confidence, and knowing when to escalate vs. when to close independently.

Account health

You track adoption rates, seat growth, and health signals, and you act on them before they become problems. You define what a healthy GfW account looks like and hold that standard across your portfolio.

Enterprise stakeholder relationships

You maintain executive-level relationships (VP IT, CIO, CTO, CPO, Head of Procurement) alongside operational contacts. You run business reviews that feel strategic, not transactional. You're the person enterprise stakeholders call when something matters — not just when something breaks.

Product expertise

GfW is an early-stage product relative to Gigs core. You are an expert in the Product and understand how to track performance to a sophisticated degree. Your accounts will surface feature gaps, deployment friction, and new use cases. You feed those back into the product team with commercial context and specificity and you're part of shaping what GfW becomes, not just managing what it is today.

 


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 5–8 years in enterprise account management, strategic partnerships, or customer success, ideally in B2B SaaS, HR tech, managed mobility, or enterprise connectivity

 - Commercial ownership: you've personally held NRR, ARR, or renewal targets, not just been adjacent to them. We'll ask for specifics.

 - Stakeholder complexity: comfortable owning relationships with multiple senior buyers in large organisations (HR, IT, Procurement, Finance, C-suite), ideally across more than one function simultaneously

 - Product fluency: you don't need to be an engineer, but enterprise connectivity deployments require enough technical understanding to earn credibility with IT and procurement buyers

 - Clear, structured external communication: exec updates and business reviews are a core part of the role

 - AI-native working style: you default to AI to accelerate account research, prep, reporting and comms. This is a hard bar at Gigs — "occasionally use it for writing" is not the profile.

 - Stage fit: there is no playbook here. GfW is building in real time. You need to be comfortable running accounts without infrastructure, and comfortable building that infrastructure as you go.

 - A genuine interest in the product: Gigs is technical, and GfW sits at the edge of HR, IT, and telecom. Candidates who are curious about how it works — not just what it does — will go further.

 

Salary Range:

US: $155,000 - $185,000 basic - UK: £80,000 - £95,000 basic

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)

jobs.title: Strategic Partnerships, UK
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

As a senior member of Gigs' UK Partnerships team, you'll lead the charge to land Gigs' next wave of banking and fintech partners in the UK. You'll own a focused list of target accounts end to end and draw on your knowledge of how large institutions actually make decisions to find and close the right partnership opportunities.

What You Will Do

 - Partnership Development: Lead end-to-end conversations with target banks and fintechs, from first outreach through deal structuring and commercial negotiation. Build relationships with decision makers across product, risk and innovation teams at target accounts.

 - Strategic Planning: Build and run the go-to-market plan for landing UK fintechs and banks. Map target accounts, find the right entry points, and design partnership structures that work for both sides.

 - Pipeline Management: Own a focused list of 10 to 20 target accounts end to end. Prioritize based on strategic fit, revenue potential, and how fast a deal can actually move.

 - Commercial Strategy: Structure commercial terms that fit large institutions' procurement and risk processes while protecting Gigs' economics. Work with legal and finance to get deals signed.

 - Cross-functional Leadership: Partner with GTM, Connectivity, and Partner Success to shape what Gigs offers bank partners. Contribute directly to UK&I market strategy, working closely with the market lead on priorities and positioning.

 - Own the number: You carry a revenue target for your account list. Success in your first 18 months looks like 2–3 signed bank or major fintech partnerships, with a qualified pipeline behind them.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You're a proven deal-maker: you've closed complex, strategic partnerships with large banks, financial institutions, or fintechs that sell into them. You know how to navigate long enterprise sales cycles and build consensus across stakeholder groups.

 - You carry real commercial weight: 8+ years in enterprise B2B commercial roles, carrying quota or revenue targets, comfortable owning results end to end.

 - You have executive presence: you can walk into a room with C-suite bank executives and hold your own.

 - You're a highly autonomous operator: you thrive as an individual contributor, building your own pipeline without a team to lean on.

 - You think strategically: you can build an account plan, defend it under scrutiny, and adjust it as you learn.

 - You're a builder at heart: you're comfortable operating without a big company machine behind you. You roll up your sleeves, from writing the deck to chasing the signature.

 - Nice to have: a background at a startup that has sold into big banks.

 - Nice to have: existing relationships or insider knowledge of major UK banks.

jobs.title: Partner Manager - Enterprise Solutions
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Gigs for Work is Gigs' enterprise offering - we help businesses give their employees access to world-class connectivity. We're looking for a Partner Manager to own the commercial success of our GfW enterprise accounts: ensuring partners launch well, grow fast, and stay.

This is a high-ownership, relationship-heavy role sitting at the intersection of commercial, product and operations. You'll be the primary relationship owner for a portfolio of enterprise GfW accounts, taking accounts from launch through to expansion, renewal and strategic planning. You're stepping into a nascent existing book of business, with a chance to play a fundemental role at the beginning of the development of this critical vertical.

The GfW motion is distinct from Gigs' core partner model. Your counterparts aren't product teams embedding connectivity into consumer apps, they're HR leads, IT directors, procurement teams and C-suite at enterprises deploying connectivity across their workforce. You need to speak their language, understand how they measure success, and make Gigs a strategic vendor in every account.

 


WHAT YOU WILL DO

Commercial ownership

You hold the number. NRR and ARR across your GfW account portfolio are yours to grow. That means proactively identifying expansion opportunities (new employee cohorts, new geographies, new use cases), running renewal conversations with confidence, and knowing when to escalate vs. when to close independently.

Account health

You track adoption rates, seat growth, and health signals, and you act on them before they become problems. You define what a healthy GfW account looks like and hold that standard across your portfolio.

Enterprise stakeholder relationships

You maintain executive-level relationships (VP IT, CIO, CTO, CPO, Head of Procurement) alongside operational contacts. You run business reviews that feel strategic, not transactional. You're the person enterprise stakeholders call when something matters — not just when something breaks.

Product expertise

GfW is an early-stage product relative to Gigs core. You are an expert in the Product and understand how to track performance to a sophisticated degree. Your accounts will surface feature gaps, deployment friction, and new use cases. You feed those back into the product team with commercial context and specificity and you're part of shaping what GfW becomes, not just managing what it is today.

 


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 5–8 years in enterprise account management, strategic partnerships, or customer success, ideally in B2B SaaS, HR tech, managed mobility, or enterprise connectivity

 - Commercial ownership: you've personally held NRR, ARR, or renewal targets, not just been adjacent to them. We'll ask for specifics.

 - Stakeholder complexity: comfortable owning relationships with multiple senior buyers in large organisations (HR, IT, Procurement, Finance, C-suite), ideally across more than one function simultaneously

 - Product fluency: you don't need to be an engineer, but enterprise connectivity deployments require enough technical understanding to earn credibility with IT and procurement buyers

 - Clear, structured external communication: exec updates and business reviews are a core part of the role

 - AI-native working style: you default to AI to accelerate account research, prep, reporting and comms. This is a hard bar at Gigs — "occasionally use it for writing" is not the profile.

 - Stage fit: there is no playbook here. GfW is building in real time. You need to be comfortable running accounts without infrastructure, and comfortable building that infrastructure as you go.

 - A genuine interest in the product: Gigs is technical, and GfW sits at the edge of HR, IT, and telecom. Candidates who are curious about how it works — not just what it does — will go further.

 

Salary Range:

US: $155,000 - $185,000 basic - UK: £80,000 - £95,000 basic

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)

jobs.title: Brand Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

We're looking for someone to define the category we're building, and Gigs' place inside it.

Reporting to our Head of Marketing, you'll shape how Gigs shows up in the world: what we say, how we say it, and where our story lands. Today we call what we do embedded connectivity. As the business grows, that framing is already starting to strain. Finding the language that replaces it, and making it stick with customers, press, investors, and partners, is the heart of this role.

But naming a category is only half the job. The other half is positioning Gigs inside it, so that when the space does have a name, we're the company people associate with it. You'll do that through our founders' voices, the stages we choose to be on, and a story that flexes across every market we operate in, because it won't land the same way in New York as it does in Paris or Singapore.

It's a build-from-scratch role for someone who has done this before and wants to do it again, at speed.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Define the category. Take us beyond "embedded connectivity" to language that holds as the business expands. You'll own the positioning, the terminology, and the argument for why this category exists at all; then get customers, press, analysts, and partners using our words.

 - Position Gigs within it. Creating a category you don't own is a gift to your competitors. You'll make sure the story we tell about the space and the story we tell about Gigs reinforce each other at every touchpoint.

 - Elevate our founders' voices. Partner directly with our founders and execs to ghostwrite and co-create thought leadership: essays, keynotes, podcasts, social, interviews; so their public voice carries the category argument rather than running parallel to it. You'll bring a point of view and the judgment to push back, respectfully.

 - Decide where we show up. Own the external calendar across conferences, stages, podcasts, newsletters, and press. Which rooms matter, which don't, and who from Gigs belongs in each one.

 - Adapt the story by market. We're growing across the US, Europe, and Asia, and the same narrative won't work everywhere. You'll figure out what travels, what needs reframing, and where we need a different approach entirely.

 - Hold the bar with Design. Partner closely with Design so the look and feel of the brand stays sharp and consistent across every format: site, deck, stage, social, event.

 - Work across the company. Growth marketing, Product, Partner Marketing, and our partners themselves all carry pieces of our story. You'll keep them coherent, and use partner surfaces as a distribution channel for the category narrative.

 - Direct the wider mix. Set the brief for and evaluate performance, events, AI-driven, and internal-communications work, going deep where it matters most and directing specialists and agencies everywhere else.

 - Put AI to work. Use AI tools day-to-day to sharpen speed, creativity, and decision-making, and help shape how Gigs is represented, discovered, and recommended across LLMs and emerging AI-driven channels.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You've created a category before. You've made a company legible before its category had a name; think explaining Uber in 2013 or Airbnb in 2011. You know the difference between a clever tagline and a frame that competitors, press, and customers actually adopt.

 - You've positioned a company inside a category, not just built one. You understand that defining the space and winning it are two separate jobs, and you've done both.

 - You've worked directly with founders. You've ghostwritten or built the public voice of a founder or executive, you're at home in the room with leadership, and you can hold your own when you disagree.

 - You're a writer by trade. An exceptional written and verbal communicator, most likely with a content strategy background. Your instinct for language is what sets you apart.

 - You've built distribution that works. You've stood up content and distribution engines that measurably grew brand awareness, and you have opinions about which stages, shows, and channels are worth the effort.

 - You've told a story across markets. You've adapted a brand narrative for different regions and know when to translate versus when to rebuild.

 - You can direct the full mix. Content, social, events, comms, design — you can set the brief and evaluate the work across all of it, even where you're not the hands-on expert. Comfort with data is a plus, but this role is judged on voice and category instinct more than dashboards.

 - You use AI in your daily work to improve speed, creativity, and decision-making.

 - You've done this in a high-growth tech startup or agency environment.

 

Salary range: $180,000 - $240,000 annually + equity

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)

jobs.title: People Business Partner
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

We’re hiring our first People Business Partner to help define what People partnering looks like at Gigs.

At Gigs, we believe that our People team exists to help the business succeed through its people. We partner closely with leaders to build exceptional teams, make thoughtful people decisions, and create the conditions for our people to do their best work. You’ll be a trusted thought partner to our org leads and managers, deeply understanding their business, priorities, and challenges and helping them navigate the people and organizational decisions that matter most.

This is not a traditional HRBP role. You’ll work across organizational design, talent strategy, performance, manager coaching, employee relations, career development, and organizational effectiveness, while also building the People infrastructure we need to scale, from leveling and career paths to performance, manager enablement, onboarding, and talent programs.

This is a builder role with significant ownership. We’re not looking to import a playbook; we want you to identify what will have the greatest impact, build what Gigs needs, and own it from strategy through execution.

The timing is intentional: our people are hungry for more. Employees are looking for more structure, clarity, and support to grow their careers, while our managers and org leads are eager for a strong thought partner as their teams and challenges become more complex. We’re at a point where investing meaningfully in both can have an outsized impact on the business.

Salary range:

 - US: $220,000 - 280,000

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)


WHAT YOU WILL DO

Partner with leaders to build exceptional teams

 - Serve as a trusted advisor to org leads and managers on talent, organizational design, performance, and team effectiveness.

 - Translate business strategy and goals into thoughtful decisions about organization, roles, capabilities, and talent.

 - Coach managers at all levels on leadership, feedback, performance, team dynamics, and employee development.

 - Partner with leaders on talent reviews, development, promotions, succession, and retention of exceptional talent.

 - Navigate employee relations and organizational change with sound judgment, empathy, and rigor.

 - Use qualitative and quantitative data to diagnose problems, identify trends, and proactively surface opportunities and risks.

Build the People systems Gigs needs to scale

 - Design and evolve our leveling and career framework, creating clear expectations and meaningful paths for growth.

 - Build and improve performance management, talent, and manager development programs.

 - Shape key parts of the employee experience, including onboarding, engagement, and other People programs as the company evolves.

 - Partner across the People team to turn business and employee insights into programs that meaningfully improve how we work.

 - Use AI, automation, and better systems to eliminate repetitive work, create leverage, and rethink how People work gets done.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of HR/People experience, including meaningful People Partner/HRBP experience in a high-growth technology company.

 - Experience partnering closely with leaders and managers across functions and levels.

 - Strong business acumen and genuine curiosity about how businesses operate, grow, and win.

 - Deep experience across organizational design, talent, performance, manager coaching, and employee development.

 - Experience building or evolving career frameworks, leveling, talent processes, or other People infrastructure.

 - Excellent judgment, coaching, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to navigate sensitive and ambiguous situations.

 - A first-principles, builder’s mindset: you’re comfortable creating from scratch, questioning existing playbooks, and rolling up your sleeves to get the work done.

 - Strong analytical skills and an interest in using AI and automation to make People work more effective and scalable.

 - Knowledge of employment law and employee relations is preferred.

jobs.title: Business Development, Technology Partnerships
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

As a senior member of the GTM team at Gigs, you'll spearhead the acquisition and growth of strategic partnerships with the world's leading technology companies looking to embed connectivity into their products. The biggest consumer technology companies across marketplaces, social platforms, vertical SaaS, and AI platforms own massive, engaged audiences and are searching for subscription value, retention levers, and new margin.

You'll lead first-of-a-kind, revenue-oriented deals with these companies, working closely with our GM of US Consumer and a dedicated cross-functional team. You'll be responsible for building our customer pipeline, structuring innovative commercial partnerships, and seeing that our relationships drive business growth. You'll leverage your deep understanding of the consumer technology ecosystem and strong commercial acumen to identify and capture opportunities, including new waves in technology (such as agentic commerce) that will change consumer buying behavior.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Partnership Execution: Lead end-to-end partnership discussions with leading technology companies, from initial outreach through deal structuring and commercial negotiations. These are pioneering deals with no established playbook, so you'll build and maintain senior relationships across product, operations, and business functions, while establishing repeatable engagement and qualification processes to support scale.

 - Strategic Planning: Develop and execute the go-to-market strategy for the vertical. Identify target segments and partnership archetypes (membership programs, marketplaces, vertical SaaS, AI platforms), craft compelling value propositions, and design scalable partnership structures and playbooks that enable consistent execution and long-term growth.

 - Pipeline Management: Build, operationalize, and continuously optimize a robust partnership funnel across technology subsegments and use cases. Implement clear qualification criteria, stage definitions, and prioritization frameworks based on strategic fit, revenue potential, and implementation complexity.

 - Commercial Strategy: Structure creative, scalable commercial models that align with partners' business objectives while capturing durable value for Gigs. Partner with legal and finance to standardize deal structures, streamline contracting, and enable faster deal velocity as the pipeline scales.

 - Cross-functional Leadership: Work closely with internal teams to operationalize partnerships pre and post-signature and ensure successful onboarding and expansion. Translate market and partner insights into actionable feedback to inform roadmap priorities and process improvements.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You're a proven deal-maker: You have a track record of closing complex, strategic, revenue-oriented partnerships with leading technology companies. You're comfortable pursuing first-of-a-kind deals where the playbook doesn't yet exist, and beyond getting deals done, you know how to systemize sourcing, qualification, and negotiation to support predictable, repeatable growth across an enterprise sales cycle.

 - You understand consumer technology: You have deep knowledge of the consumer technology ecosystem, including key players, business models, and industry trends. You can speak credibly about subscription and membership economics, platform monetization, retention strategy, and emerging shifts like agentic commerce that will reshape how consumers buy.

 - You're commercially creative: You can structure innovative partnership models that create win-win scenarios. You're comfortable with complex commercial terms and can translate partner needs into viable deal structures.

 - You're analytically strong: You can build detailed business cases, model partnership economics, and use data to drive decision-making. You understand unit economics and can evaluate partnership opportunities quantitatively.

 - You're a strategic collaborator: You work effectively with internal stakeholders, particularly program management, to ensure alignment between commercial promises and implementation capabilities. You're known for creating clarity, building trust, and driving outcomes through structured collaboration and operational rigor.

 

Salary range: $180,000 - $260,000 annually + variable + equity

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)
